newsitem.title: USA: ABC upfront ad market rises to $1.6 bln.
newsitem.headline: ABC upfront ad market rises to $1.6 bln.

text.p: Walt Disney Co's ABC Television unit on Wednesday said it generated $1.6 billion in advance advertising sales for the new primetime TV season, compared with $1.5 billion in so-called upfront sales last year.
Primetime ad rates rose seven to eight percent over last year's rates, said Marvin Goldsmith, president of ABC television network sales and marketing.
In the so-called fringe market, daytime ad sales totaled $510 million, up about $10 million from last year, he said.
Goldsmith confirmed industry reports that the network moved more quickly than its rivals to sell upfront time rather than waiting for demand to surface in the remaining scattered market.

Among the four networks, the network finished third in last season's ratings race in terms of average household audience, leading ABC to lock up as much upfront revenue as it could, industry observers said.
Goldsmith said the network sold out about 85 percent of its commercial time, up from 75 percent last year.
He said automotive, packaged goods, retailing and fast food chains were the strongest categories.
